messages:
Kai (customer): Hey team — we pushed an update and since ~08:15 UTC we’re seeing much higher TTFB for streaming responses vs non-streaming. Total time is similar, but first chunk is delayed by ~800-1200ms. Affects customers on EU region behind our proxy. Request-id: req_32ab9. Sample curl attached.
Mike (Support): sorry you hit this, can you paste a minimal curl/request and confirm protocol (h2 vs SSE) and model?
Kai (customer): Using h2 (gRPC-like http2 streaming) to /v1/responses, model redwood-v1, payload size small. cURL: `curl -v --http2 -H "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/responses`
Kai (customer): Also noticed that if we call the non-streaming endpoint (blocking), first byte is ~60ms. Streaming first byte ~1.1s.
Mike (Support): thanks. tagging eng-runtime @Lucy and SRE @Jana.
Lucy (Eng-Runtime): thanks @Mike. tagging infra-bot to check any proxy coalescing/fanout changes in EU around that time.
infra-bot: deploy event: rolling-proxy-update-eu completed at 1769989950 by ops-deploy. Changelog: "tune http2 connection settings, enable coalescing for small frames"
Jana (SRE): that deploy timestamp lines up. We’ve seen coalescing improvements for throughput but can increase TTFB for small streaming chunks. Can we get a trace (tcpdump or request flow) and the exact timing of frames?
Kai (customer): attaching timeline: connect 40ms, TLS handshake 12ms, request headers 28ms, server processing immediate, first data delivered from origin 50ms, but client sees first data at +1100ms.
Mike (Support): so origin writes quickly but something in path delays chunk flush. Likely proxy coalescing or buffer flush heuristic. Lucy any recent change to streaming flush heuristics?
Lucy (Eng-Runtime): we didn’t change runtime flush. Infra change matches. Our runtime sends chunks with `flush(true)` per token. If the proxy groups small frames into larger ones or waits for a larger write window, that explains it.
Jana (SRE): quick mitigation options: 1) rollback proxy coalescing flag, 2) force server-side larger initial chunk (padding), 3) route affected customers to dedicated path that disables coalescing. Which is acceptable short-term?
Kai (customer): 2 is risky for us — padding changes semantics. 1 or 3 preferred. 3 would be ideal if it’s fast.
Lucy (Eng-Runtime): we can add a temporary header `x-rw-stream-flush: immediate` that bypasses proxy coalescing if the proxy honors it. Will need infra to accept header.
Jana (SRE): ops: can we add header whitelist on proxy? @ops-team
Mike (Support): ops pinged. Meanwhile can the customer switch to non-streaming as short stopgap?
Kai (customer): non-streaming works but we lose early tokens. We’d prefer streaming.
ops (ops-team via infra-bot): added header whitelist at 1769990022 for `x-rw-stream-flush`. Will accept and bypass coalescing for whitelisted requests.
Lucy (Eng-Runtime): we rolled a small patch to include header when client indicates streaming mode. Patch posted. Example client instruct: add header `x-rw-stream-prefer-flush: 1` to the request.
Kai (customer): tested with header — TTFB dropped to ~70ms. Nice. Can you explain root cause?
Jana (SRE): root cause: proxy coalescing enabled in recent rollout groups small server frames until either N bytes or timeout t_elapsed. That improved throughput for many workloads but increased TTFB for low-throughput streaming (first token). The proxy change lacked per-route opt-outs.
Lucy (Eng-Runtime): long-term fixes: 1) make runtime emit slightly larger initial chunk for HTTP2 without changing token semantics (merge metadata+first token), 2) add a streaming hint header by default for client SDKs, 3) tune proxy coalescing heuristics to be content-aware.
Mike (Support): action items: - ops to monitor any rollback effects (Jana) - eng-runtime to ship header + SDK updates (Lucy) - support to inform customers and provide quick header workaround (Mike)
Jana (SRE): monitoring: created grafana panel and alert for streaming TTFB p95/p99 by region. Alert threshold: p95 > 300ms or p99 > 800ms.
deploy-bot: canary rollback requested by ops at 1769990055: rolling-proxy-update-eu -> rollback init
Jana (SRE): we started rollback; will confirm when complete.
Kai (customer): appreciate the quick triage and hotfix. Will hold on full rollout until we see stable TTFB.
Mike (Support): closing loop: please paste any additional request-ids if you see anomalies. We'll follow up with postmortem once rollback and header patch are live. :thumbsup:
